result.title: Test-Time Scaling for Open-Ended Reasoning at Small Model Scale
result.summary: A vote over a model's samples can only help when the samples disagree. For open-ended generation the binding question is therefore not how to combine samples but whether a model produces samples worth combining, a question test-time scaling has answered for math but not for free-form text. We study it at small scale with semantic cluster voting, a judge-free aggregator that groups a small instruct model's samples by meaning and returns the largest cluster's representative, with no reward model or self-judging. On a 250-prompt benchmark with three tiers of answer checkability, the same pattern holds across three model families (Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-3B, Gemma-2-2B) and two generation seeds: voting raises accuracy on the math control, where samples vary but stay checkable (a gain of +10 to +29 points across the three models), yet adds at most +0.30 judge points on open-ended text. On a larger 200-problem MATH-500 run with the primary model, the math gain is +8.5 points (95% CI [+4.0, +13.0]). Almost every open-ended sample falls into one meaning cluster, so there is little to select over. The collapse is consistent with instruction-tuning rather than model size, and raising decoding temperature does not recover usable diversity, because it costs more quality than it adds (net -0.64 judge points, 95% CI [-0.93, -0.37]).

AI.brief_summary: 论文在小模型上检验 test-time scaling 对开放式生成是否有效，提出按语义聚类、无需奖励模型或自评判的语义聚类投票聚合器，并在三层可核查性基准与三个模型家族上比较数学与自由文本的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「样本是否值得组合」的诊断与无监督聚类聚合方式，可供核查并行 latent 假设聚合时的多样性坍缩与收益边界；论文发现开放式文本几乎全部落入单一语义簇、提高温度反而净损质量，这一负结果可能提示多假设推理需先评估采样多样性。
